problem.statement: WPF's binding engine silently falls back to a PropertyDescriptor.AddValueChanged listener when binding to properties that don't implement INotifyPropertyChanged, and these listeners are never released, causing long-lived binding memory leaks.

persona.primary: WPF developer diagnosing memory leaks in a legacy WPF/.NET application

context.situation: A WPF developer profiling their application's memory usage discovered that bindings to properties on immutable/non-INPC models silently create leaking PropertyDescriptor listeners, a framework behavior that has existed for years and is undocumented to most developers.

current_workarounds: Implementing INotifyPropertyChanged on every bound model/property to avoid triggering the PropertyDescriptor fallback path (implied by the poster's stated goal of avoiding this requirement)
existing_substitutes: Snoop (WPF visual tree/binding debugger, used to detect the leak)
dotMemory (JetBrains .NET memory profiler, used to diagnose the leak per referenced blog post)

possible_wedges.offer: A static analyzer/CLI that scans XAML + code-behind for Binding/PropertyPath usages targeting non-INotifyPropertyChanged properties and flags them as likely PropertyDescriptor leak risks.
A Visual Studio/Roslyn analyzer that lints WPF bindings at build time and warns when a bound property lacks INPC and will trigger the leaking fallback.
A Snoop-style runtime inspector focused specifically on surfacing active PropertyDescriptor.AddValueChanged listeners and their retaining objects for legacy WPF apps.

risks: Single evidence item (n=1); no corroborating reports of prevalence or severity across other teams
Evidence is a framework bug-fix proposal on GitHub, not a product inquiry — near-zero commercial intent signal (0.05) and zero commitment signal
No workarounds or willingness-to-pay evidence beyond the poster's own suggested framework-level fix
Poster's own preferred solution is a free upstream WPF engine fix, which could obsolete any paid tooling wedge
WPF/legacy .NET is a shrinking, niche developer population, limiting addressable market size

cheapest_experiment.hypothesis: WPF developers maintaining legacy codebases would engage with a free, lightweight scanner that flags bindings likely to trigger the PropertyDescriptor leak, indicating demand for a fuller audit tool.
cheapest_experiment.input: A short blog post/landing page (or GitHub gist) offering a free static-analysis script that scans XAML files for bindings to non-INotifyPropertyChanged properties, shared in the same WPF GitHub issue thread and relevant WPF/.NET forums.
cheapest_experiment.output: Count of signups, repo stars/forks, downloads, or inbound comments/questions requesting more capability.
cheapest_experiment.commitment_event: Visitor provides an email address or stars/forks the repo to access the scanner.
cheapest_experiment.success_threshold: 15+ signups or stars within 2 weeks from WPF-specific channels.
cheapest_experiment.failure_threshold: Fewer than 5 signups/stars and no unprompted follow-up questions after 2 weeks.
